items.title: mltreelib
items.text:
Tree-based machine learning with a Rust core. A data and feature layer that treats missing data as first-class, an adjustable benchmark generator with known ground truth, and — next — tree learners that handle categoricals and missing values natively. The research bet: the signal hidden in categorical, grouped and hierarchical structure is what flat learners lose, and it can be measured.

  • Rust core (mltreelib-core), thin Python shell (PyO3); R planned
  • Scikit-learn-shaped API — without the scikit-learn dependency
  • NA and NaN handled end-to-end: missing in → missing out; imputation opt-in
  • 51 TabArena-v0.1 benchmark datasets on board, plus a generator whose knobs control how much signal lives in group and hierarchy structure
uv sync                                # venv + Rust extension (maturin)
uv run pytest tests/ -q                # behavior tests
uv run python examples/data_layer_demo.py   # see everything on real data

The research program, roadmap and contribution rules live in the repository (README.md, AGENTS.md).

Try it right now

uv run python examples/data_layer_demo.py churn prints ingest, missingness, encodings, grouped/trended/windowed/decomposed features and the generator's ground truth — all on a real dataset.

items.title: Benchmark datasets
items.text:
datasets/ holds the full TabArena-v0.1 suite: 51 curated tabular datasets (87.4 MB, OpenML suite 457) — 7 regression, 44 classification, 4 small (<1k rows), 40 medium, 7 large (up to 150k rows), including high-cardinality categorical sets. Files are parquet with categoricals preserved as strings; datasets/MANIFEST.md lists per-dataset target, size, license and source.

from mltreelib import list_datasets, load_dataset

list_datasets()                 # ['APSFailure', 'Bank_Customer_Churn', ...]
ds = load_dataset("churn")
ds["n_rows"], ds["n_cols"]      # 5000, 20
ds["dtypes"]                    # {"state": "categorical", "account_length": "numeric", ...}
ds["na_counts"]                 # missing shown by default

load_dataset returns the same shape as DatasetBuilder.build(), so it feeds straight back into the data layer.

BeyondArena

The beyond-IID extension (temporal/grouped splits) ships via the separate data-foundry package and is intentionally not vendored; see the manifest for notes.

items.title: Field notes: what it actually costs to just run a tree
items.text: Building the Elo arena meant wiring up every major tree/model-tree implementation. The friction is the point of this page: mltreelib is one import with zero transitive quirks, and this is what the alternatives cost.
path: Field notes: what it actually costs to just run a tree

items.title: The hassle log (all real, all this week)
items.text: what what happened perpetual (Rust GBM) imports sklearn internally — install fails at runtime without scikit-learn, error surfaces only on first fit ctboost sklearn-style estimators refuse to import without scikit-learn ("ctboost scikit-learn estimators require scikit-learn") catboost 92MB wheel; on a slow link the whole benchmark blocks on the download forust (Rust GBM) regression objective is objective_type="SquaredLoss" — "SquaredError" raises ValueError; the name is only in the API docs R Cubist the function is cubist() (lowercase) though the class is Cubist R grf local_linear_forest was renamed ll_regression_forest in 2.x; lm_forest is a causal forest that demands W; predict is S3, not grf::predict R packages on this box site-library not writable → R_LIBS_USER + user library dance sklearn trees cannot consume NAs at all — mean-imputation required before fit PyPI/README hunting install names ≠ import names (py-forust vs forust), example fences not greppable, bot-blocked pages
path: Field notes: what it actually costs to just run a tree

items.title: What our side of the page looks like
items.text:
from mltreelib import ModelTree            # that is the install story
m = ModelTree(leaf="linear")               # or leaf="mean", leaf_cols="path"
m.fit(x, y)                                # x may contain None — NAs first-class
m.predict(x)                               # never fails on a missing value
m.leaves()[0]                              # coef, na_coef, mean, std, quantiles
m.profile()                                # per-level timings built in
  • one dependency family (Rust core + thin Python shell);
  • NAs are first-class (learned split directions, NA-indicator leaf terms);
  • every leaf keeps its statistics and a t-digest;
  • the tree reproduces rpart exactly when configured as CART (mean leaves), so results are checkable against the reference implementations.

items.title: How the Elo works (our protocol)
items.text:
Elo comes from chess: every model carries a rating; when two models "play", the winner takes points from the loser proportionally to how surprising the result was.

  • Expected score of A against B: E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^((R_B - R_A) / 400)) (equal ratings → 50%; a 200-point underdog still expects ~24%).
  • After a game with actual score S_A (1 win, 0.5 draw, 0 loss): R_A += K * (S_A - E_A), R_B += K * (S_B - E_B), with K = 32 here.

What counts as a game: on each dataset, every unordered pair of models plays once — lower RMSE wins (equal RMSE = draw). So 16 datasets × n·(n-1)/2 games per full field. The order is deterministic (datasets sorted, pairs lexicographic), so the whole board is reproducible from the score file.

How to read it:

  • Ratings are relative — the zero point moves when models enter or leave (the same tree scored 901 with 13 models and 858 with 18). Watch the ordering and the gaps, not the absolute numbers.
  • One model with several flavors (our three leaf kinds) splits its own wins — treat them as separate competitors, which is intended.
  • K = 32 keeps the board responsive to real differences; over 5 datasets a genuinely better model climbs fast.
  • TabArena's numbers are not comparable — different protocol (their own tournament + bootstrapping on 51 datasets incl. classification). They are a scale anchor only.

Reproduce: elo_prepare.py (data, once) → elo_score_r.R → elo_score_python.py → elo_score_rust.py (each environment, incremental upsert) → elo_report.py (this Elo computation).

items.title: The Elo board (arena run, stock configs)
items.text:
Five real regression sets (concrete, abalone, ozone, boston, fc2008), one 80/20 split each, identical encodings; round-robin Elo on per-dataset RMSE (K=32, start 1000). Reproduce: elo_prepare.py → elo_score_r.R → elo_score_python.py → elo_score_rust.py → elo_report.py; the numbers live in benchmarks/elo_scores.csv.

Elo model note 1418.7 CatBoost (200) best on fc2008 and boston 1327.0 forust (Rust) 1216.0 grf local-linear forest fc2008 NAs defeat it (4/5) 1212.8 LightGBM (200) 1202.3 perpetual (Rust) 1129.3 CTBoost ctree-based GBDT 1092.0 Cubist (R) the C5-family regressor 1081.0 grf RF 972.8 earth (MARS) cannot take NAs (4/5) 963.1 glmtree (partykit) 948.4 modeltrees lmtree matches partykit to 3 decimals - port certified 945.6 lmtree (partykit) 884.9 ctree (partykit) 867.9 sklearn tree needs mean-imputation for NAs 858.2 ModelTree(mean) — ours unoptimized defaults 714.9 rpart 597.0 ModelTree(path) — ours 568.2 ModelTree(all) — ours unregularized leaves blow up on fc2008

Reference scale (different protocol): TabArena best overall Kumo-Tabular 1955; best tree-based LightGBM tuned+ens 1411.

The board is the yardstick: every default change, leaf variant, and forest feature moves these numbers, and examples/default_search.py bakes the winning defaults against the lmtree/cubist/rpart bars.

items.title: Why this page exists
items.text: Benchmarks should be about models, not plumbing. The Elo arena (examples/elo_prepare.py → elo_score_r.R / elo_score_python.py / elo_score_rust.py → elo_report.py, one scores file) exists so the field can be re-run incrementally — but assembling it highlighted how much incidental complexity the alternatives impose. That complexity is our documentation.

items.title: Data layer
items.text:
Ingest any data with the semantics that matter: category inference, explicit NA policies, digit rounding, optional intercept.

from mltreelib import DatasetBuilder

b = DatasetBuilder(n_category=0.05, na_policy="impute", digits=2, add_intercept=True)
b.add_numeric("price", [1.234, None, 2.356])
b.add_categorical("region", ["north", "south", None])
ds = b.build()
ds["n_rows"], ds["dtypes"], ds["na_counts"]

Missing values are None or NaN — both are missing, counted in na_counts, and filling is never implicit (allow / drop / impute).

items.title: Summaries and encodings
items.text:
from mltreelib import summarize, IndexMapper

summarize([1.0, None, 3.0])   # count, n_missing, mean, std, min, q1, median, q3, max

m = IndexMapper()
m.fit("region", ["north", "south", "north"])
m.transform("region", ["north", "unseen"])   # [0, None] — unseen levels are missing

items.title: Feature transforms
items.text:
from mltreelib import GroupedScaler, VariableScaler, grouped_transform

grouped_transform(keys, values, kind="mean")        # per-group summary per row
g = GroupedScaler(); g.fit(keys, values, "zscore"); g.transform(keys, values)
v = VariableScaler(); v.fit({"price": prices}, "min-max")   # per-column, exact inverse

18 distributional strategies (zscore, min-max, median-iqr, min-qd, … and the ratio family), all with algebraic inverse_transform.

items.title: Time features
items.text:
from mltreelib import calendar_features, lag_by_days, trended_transform, windowed_transform, decomposed_transform

calendar_features(["2026-10-28"])                  # weekday, season, ISO week, ...
lag_by_days(keys, dates, values, 7)                # day lags within each key
trended_transform(keys, dates, values, granularity="year_month")
windowed_transform(keys, dates, values, window_days=7, kind="sum")
decomposed_transform(keys, dates, values, season_granularity="weekday", trend_window=7)

Decomposition follows the statsmodels seasonal_decompose (additive) convention: detrended, deseasonalized, residual. Time-series transforms drop incomplete rows and raise a UserWarning with the count.

items.title: Generator with ground truth
items.text:
from mltreelib import generate

g = generate(n_rows=10_000, cardinalities=[8, 64], hierarchy_levels=2,
             group_effect_strength=0.6, seed=42)
g["truth"]["variance"]   # realized variance share per component

Every learner can be scored on structure recovery, not just accuracy.

items.title: DatasetBuilder
items.text:
class DatasetBuilder(n_category=None, na_policy='allow', digits=None, add_intercept=False)

Ingest any data into the typed dataset.

Owns the ingestion semantics: n_category category inference, explicit NA policy, digit rounding and an optional intercept column. Missing is None or NaN — both are counted in na_counts, and filling is opt-in only.

Args (constructor): n_category: integral numeric columns with at most this many distinct levels become categorical; values < 1 mean a fraction of rows (None = no inference). na_policy: "allow" (keep missing), "drop" (drop rows containing any missing) or "impute" (numeric mean, categorical mode). digits: round floats to this many decimal places (None = no rounding). add_intercept: append a constant 1.0 column named intercept.

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_categorical
items.text:
add_categorical(self, /, name, values)

Add a categorical column from strings; the vocabulary is first-seen order. None = missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one level per row (None = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_numeric
items.text:
add_numeric(self, /, name, values)

Add a numeric column. NaN is treated as missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one value per row (None/NaN = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.build
items.text:
build(self, /)

Build the typed dataset with the configured policies applied.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values), dtypes ("numeric" or "categorical"), na_counts (missing per column), n_rows, n_cols.

Raises: ValueError: inconsistent column lengths, duplicate names, invalid policy usage (e.g. "drop" removing every row).

items.title: IndexMapper
items.text:
class IndexMapper()

Categorical string <-> stable code mapping (sklearn-style fit/transform).

items.title: IndexMapper.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, name, values)

Learn the vocabulary of name (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets it.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_all_names
items.text:
get_all_names(self, /, name)

All fitted levels in code order.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_index
items.text:
get_index(self, /, name, value)

Code for one level (None when the level is unseen).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_name
items.text:
get_name(self, /, name, index)

Level for one code.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, name, codes)

Map codes back to their string levels.

Args: name: fitted column name. codes: codes per row (None = missing).

Returns: string levels (None where the code is missing).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, name, values)

Codes for values; unseen levels map to None (missing).

items.title: OneHotEncoder
items.text:
class OneHotEncoder()

One-hot expansion: one indicator column per fitted level (first-seen order). Missing values and levels unseen at fit produce an all-zero row.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Learn the levels (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets them.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.levels
items.text:
levels(self, /)

Fitted levels, in column order.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {level: indicator list}; unseen/missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: HashingEncoder
items.text:
class HashingEncoder(n_buckets)

Hashed one-hot: levels are hashed into n_buckets indicator columns, so unseen levels still land somewhere. Deterministic.

items.title: HashingEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {bucket name: indicator list}.

items.title: BaseNEncoder
items.text:
class BaseNEncoder(base)

Base-N / binary encoding: each level becomes its base-base digits as indicator columns (base = 2 is the classic Binary encoder). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen and missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {digit name: indicator list}.

items.title: CountEncoder
items.text:
class CountEncoder(normalize)

Count / frequency encoding: occurrence count per category (normalize gives the share of rows). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen levels give 0.0; missing stays missing.

items.title: CountEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit counts on values.

items.title: CountEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Count (or share) per row; unseen -> 0.0, missing -> None.

items.title: SumEncoder
items.text:
class SumEncoder()

Sum contrast coding: k-1 columns; level i < k-1 gets +1 in column i, the last level gets -1 across all columns. Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen rows give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: SumEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: SumEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Contrast row per row (None = missing).

items.title: TargetEncoder
items.text:
class TargetEncoder(smoothing)

Smoothed target encoding (fitted-mean flavour).

w * level_mean + (1 - w) * global_mean with w = n / (n + smoothing). Leaky on training data (the row's own target is in its level mean) — prefer CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform for training features. Unseen levels fall back to the global mean; missing stays missing.

items.title: TargetEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: TargetEncoder.prior
items.text:
prior(self, /)

The global mean used as the unseen-level fallback.

items.title: TargetEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Encode values; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder
items.text:
class MEstimatorEncoder(m)

M-estimate encoding: (sum_y + m * global) / (n_level + m) — target smoothing with fixed strength m. Task: both (leaky on training data; prefer CatBoostEncoder or LeaveOneOutEncoder there). Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit smoothed level means on (values, y).

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Smoothed mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder
items.text:
class LeaveOneOutEncoder()

Leave-one-out encoding: fit_transform gives each row its level's mean target without that row (leakage-aware); transform on new data uses the full fitted level mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global mean; missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit_transform
items.text:
fit_transform(self, /, values, y)

Row-level means excluding each row's own target.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Full fitted level means for new rows.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder
items.text:
class CatBoostEncoder(prior, permutations, seed)

CatBoost-style ordered target statistics — the leakage-safe flavour.

fit_transform gives each row the running statistic of its level using only rows earlier in a shuffled order: (sum_y_prefix + prior * global) / (n_prefix + 1), averaged over permutations seeded passes. The same level gets different values in different rows — that row-dependence is the anti-leakage mechanism. transform (new data) uses prior-smoothed fitted level means.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit prior-smoothed level means (used by transform on new data).

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform
items.text:
fit_transform(self, /, values, y)

Leakage-safe ordered encodings of the training rows themselves.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Encode new rows from the fitted level means; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: QuantileEncoder
items.text:
class QuantileEncoder(q, smoothing)

Quantile encoding: each level becomes its smoothed target quantile (default median), w * level_quantile + (1 - w) * global_quantile with w = n / (n + smoothing). Task: regression. Unseen -> global quantile; missing -> None.

items.title: QuantileEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit quantiles on (values, y).

items.title: QuantileEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Smoothed quantile per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder
items.text:
class JamesSteinEncoder()

James-Stein encoding: level means shrunk toward the grand mean with B = max(0, 1 - ((L - 3) * sigma2) / sum((mean_i - global)^2)); fewer than three levels collapse to the grand mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit shrunk means on (values, y).

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Shrunk mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: TfidfEncoder
items.text:
class TfidfEncoder(normalize)

Class-level TF-IDF: each category becomes a vector over the target classes — tf(v,j) = count(v,j)/count(v) times idf(j) = ln(1 + n/(1 + count(j))) + 1; normalize scales each level vector to unit L2 norm. Task: classification. Unseen levels fall back to the global class shares; missing stays missing.

items.title: TfidfEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes)

Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: TfidfEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

One class-space vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: WoEEncoder
items.text:
class WoEEncoder(prior)

Weight of Evidence (credit-risk classic): one-vs-rest ln(distr_j(v) / distr_not_j(v)) per category, smoothed with additive prior. Task: classification. Positive = over-representation of the class in that level. Unseen levels give neutral zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: WoEEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes)

Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: WoEEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

One WoE vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder
items.text:
class EmbeddingEncoder(dim, lr, epochs, seed, task)

NN-style learned embeddings per category: a small embedding table and a linear head trained by SGD, one table per categorical feature. Task: both — softmax head for classification; for regression a ReLU output when all fitted targets are non-negative, linear otherwise. transform returns the embeddings, predict the trained head. Unseen levels give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes=None)

Train on (values, y); n_classes is inferred for classification when omitted, ignored for regression.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.predict
items.text:
predict(self, /, values)

Predictions of the trained head (class label or activated value).

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Learned embedding per row (None = missing, zeros = unseen).

items.title: GroupedScaler
items.text:
class GroupedScaler()

Fit/transform group distributional scaling with exact inverse (sklearn-shaped: fit once, then transform / inverse_transform).

Strategies: centered family — "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr"; ratio family — "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range". Missing in -> missing out; degenerate (zero) scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: GroupedScaler.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, keys, values, strategy)

Fit group statistics of values under the given strategy.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; counted in each group's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see the class docstring).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, keys, values)

Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, keys, values)

Scale values against the fitted group statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: numeric value per row.

Returns: scaled values; None for missing key/value, unseen groups and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: VariableScaler
items.text:
class VariableScaler()

Per-column distributional scaling — each variable transformed independently (legacy VariableTransformation semantics).

Same strategy names as GroupedScaler, applied per column, with exact inverse_transform. None/NaN are missing and pass through as missing; degenerate scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: VariableScaler.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, columns, strategy)

Fit all columns at once under the given strategy.

Args: columns: {name: values} for every column to scale (None/NaN = missing; counted in each column's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see GroupedScaler).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy.

items.title: VariableScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, name, values)

Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: VariableScaler.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, name, values)

Scale one fitted column's values.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: scaled values; None for missing inputs and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: grouped_scale
items.text:
def grouped_scale(keys, values, strategy='zscore')

One-shot group scaling: fit on (keys, values) and transform the same rows.

Each row's value is scaled by its group's summary under strategy (centered family like "zscore" or ratio family like "mean"; see GroupedScaler for the full list and the exact inverse).

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing). strategy: one of "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr", "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range".

Returns: scaled values; rows with a missing key/value, an unseen group or a degenerate (zero) scale give None — missing in, missing out.

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: grouped_transform
items.text:
def grouped_transform(keys, values, kind='mean')

Per-row group summary of values within groups defined by keys.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; excluded from the group statistics but counted in each group's n_missing). kind: "mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1" or "q3".

Returns: the summary of each row's group; rows with a missing key/value or an unseen group give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown kind or mismatched lengths.

items.title: summarize
items.text:
def summarize(values)

Summary of observed values, with missing counts shown by default.

NAs and NaNs are excluded from the statistics but always reported in n_missing — nothing is silently hidden.

Args: values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: dict with count (observed), n_missing, sum, mean, std, min, q1, median, q3, max (NaN for the statistics of an all-missing input).

items.title: calendar_features
items.text:
def calendar_features(dates, hemisphere='north')

Calendar features for ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD or timestamp prefix).

Produces year, halfyear, quarter, month, week (ISO), iso_year, weekday (0 = Monday), day, day_of_year, season and weekend as numeric parts, ready for tree learners.

Args: dates: ISO date strings or timestamps (None = missing). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (southern shifts the season by six months).

Returns: dict of 11 feature lists aligned with dates; rows with a missing date give None features.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or unknown hemisphere.

items.title: lag_by_days
items.text:
def lag_by_days(keys, dates, values, lag_days)

Lag values by whole days within each key (day granularity).

Each row receives the value of its key at date - lag_days; duplicate (key, date) rows keep the last occurrence. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). lag_days: lag in whole days (0 returns the row's own value).

Returns: lagged values; None where no source row exists.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: trended_transform
items.text:
def trended_transform(keys, dates, values, granularity='year_month', kind='mean', hemisphere='north')

Grouped summary trended at a time granularity.

Each row gets the summary of its (key x time-bucket) cell — e.g. with granularity "year_month" and kind "mean", the row's key-and-month mean. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). granularity: bucket spec joined by "_" from {year, halfyear, season, quarter, month, week, weekday, day} — e.g. "year_month", "year_week", "month_weekday". kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: per-row cell summaries; incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown granularity/kind/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: decomposed_transform
items.text:
def decomposed_transform(keys, dates, values, season_granularity='month', trend_window=3, hemisphere='north')

Additive decomposition, following the statsmodels seasonal_decompose (additive) convention.

The trend is a centered moving average over each key's rows ordered by date; the seasonal component is the mean of (series - trend) per (key, season bucket), estimated from rows with a complete trend window. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). season_granularity: bucket spec for the seasonal component (e.g. "month", "weekday" — same vocabulary as trended_transform). trend_window: centered moving-average window in rows (>= 1). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: dict with detrended (series - trend), deseasonalized (series - seasonal) and residual (series - trend - seasonal); incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: trend_window == 0, unknown granularity/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: windowed_transform
items.text:
def windowed_transform(keys, dates, values, window_days=7, kind='mean', include_current=True)

Trailing-window aggregation per key over day windows.

Each row summarizes the observed values of its key in a window of window_days days; incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). window_days: window length in days (>= 1); covering the window_days days ending at the row's date, or strictly earlier days when include_current is false. kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). include_current: include the row's own date in the window.

Returns: per-row window summaries; None for incomplete rows and for empty/all-missing windows.

Raises: ValueError: window_days == 0, unknown kind, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: generate
items.text:
def generate(n_rows=10000, n_numeric=5, cardinalities=None, hierarchy_levels=3, branching=None, group_effect_strength=0.5, hierarchy_effect_strength=0.3, interaction_strength=0.2, noise=0.1, task='regression', n_classes=2, tail_behavior='gaussian', missingness=0.0, seed=42)

Generate an adjustable benchmark dataset with known ground truth.

The knobs control how much signal lives in numeric effects, categorical levels, hierarchical groups and their interaction — so learners can be scored on structure recovery, not just accuracy. Deterministic for a given seed.

Args: n_rows: number of rows to generate. n_numeric: numeric feature columns; the first two carry linear signal. cardinalities: level count per categorical column (each >= 2). hierarchy_levels: depth of the categorical hierarchy (0 = none). branching: child count per hierarchy level (last value repeats). group_effect_strength: scale of categorical level effects. hierarchy_effect_strength: scale of hierarchy node effects. interaction_strength: scale of the numeric x categorical interaction. noise: scale of the residual noise. task: "regression" or "classification". n_classes: class count for classification (equal-frequency cuts). tail_behavior: "gaussian", "heavy" (Student-t residuals) or "bathtub" (noise grows with the signal — the DAR motivation). missingness: fraction of feature cells set to missing, in [0, 1). seed: RNG seed.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values, None = missing), target, labels (classification only) and truth — the true effects plus truth["variance"], the realized variance share of each component.

Raises: ValueError: invalid parameter combination.

items.title: list_datasets
items.text:
def list_datasets() -> 'list[str]'

Names of the available benchmark datasets (parquet stems).

items.title: load_dataset
items.text:
def load_dataset(name: 'str') -> 'dict'

Load one dataset as name/columns/dtypes/n_rows/n_cols.

columns maps column name to a list with None for missing values; dtypes is "numeric" or "categorical" (strings/dictionaries).

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
class Metrics()

One metrics class computing complete reports at once — the yardstick every learner is measured with. Task: both. Pairs with a missing/NaN side are dropped from the math and reported in n_missing, never hidden.

items.title: Metrics.classification
items.text:
classification(self, /, y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None)

Complete classification report: accuracy, macro averages, per-class precision/recall/f1/support, confusion matrix — and with probabilities (P(class 1)) also logloss, brier and ROC-AUC.

Args: y_true: integer class labels (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: predicted labels (None/NaN = missing). probabilities: P(class 1) per row; enables the probabilistic metrics.

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths, non-integer labels or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.regression
items.text:
regression(self, /, y_true, y_pred)

Complete regression report: n, n_missing, mean_error (actual - fitted), bias (mean_pred / mean_true), mae, mad, mape (non-zero targets), rmse, r2, max_error, explained_variance and deciles — the DAR per-target-decile error profile (the bathtub view).

Args: y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.regression_by_group
items.text:
regression_by_group(self, /, keys, y_true, y_pred)

Regression report per group (keys: dates, categories, ...) — the legacy per-key summary lineage. Rows with a missing key are ignored.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = ignored). y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: {group: regression report}, sorted by group.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or a group with no observed pairs.
